name: Cathedral Basilica of the Immaculate Conception
history: Mobile's parish was founded on 20 July 1703 by the Bishop of Quebec, the first on the Gulf Coast. Bishop Michael Portier laid the cathedral's cornerstone in 1835, but the Panic of 1837 delayed it; it was consecrated in 1850 without its portico or towers. The 1865 explosion of a Union ammunition depot shattered its windows. Bishop Quinlan added the portico in the 1870s and the towers were completed in 1884. It became a basilica in 1962.
arch: A Roman basilica design by Claude Beroujon, with a classical portico of eight massive Doric columns between two towers topped by domes.
features: In 1946 a U.S. Navy plane hit the south tower before crashing nearby.
It stands on the site of the Old Spanish Burying Ground.

look.d: Added in the 1870s, decades after the church was consecrated.
Completed in 1884; one was struck by a Navy plane in 1946.

fun: The parish is older than New Orleans.
journal: The Gulf Coast's first parish, 1703. Columns added late, towers later still.
